question: Can a semantic Git merge driver eliminate .ros/ Praxis state conflicts without losing or duplicating records?
hypothesis: H1: 26/26 logged R8 conflicted PR merges complete with zero .ros/ conflicts; H2: result semantically equal to the team's merge commit, 0 lost, 0 duplicated; H3: generalizes to all .ros-conflicted merges in R8 and R10.
independentVars: merge driver: none (git ort text merge) vs ros-history driver (v1 strict, v2 relaxed-order) configured via .git/info/attributes
dependentVars: ID-set/content/order/metadata equality vs merge commit M
praxis validate exit on M and on driver result
comparison: same parents re-merged with and without the driver; driver result compared with the team-produced merge commit

startRevision.indy-init-rehearsal-008: fd8fba9 (local clone shallow; scratch clone unshallowed from GitHub)

tools: praxis native release 3.24.0 (R8 pin) and 3.25.0 (R10 pin), sha256-verified

environment.host: sandbox VM, 4 vCPU, 15 GB RAM, shared with other sprint tracks (1-min load avg 7-11 during builds)

procedure: protocols/SPR-A2-01-ros-merge-driver.md (preregistered 3e11073; Amendment 1 after v1 replay). For each target merge M: checkout P1, `git merge --no-ff --no-commit P2` without then with the driver; compare driver output for each .ros history file with M; separately commit the driver result (non-.ros conflicted files taken from M) and run `praxis validate` on it and on M.

files: raw/replay-r8-all86-v2.jsonl (shallow clone; SUPERSEDED, one invalid replay)

r10All34V2.idSetEqualToM: 67/68 files (exception: M d8447ed1 dropped WI-0003; driver kept it)

validate.onM: 33/34 pass (d8447ed1 fails: linked work item WI-0003 not present)

rawResults.otherRehearsals: git merge-tree over all 2-parent merges: R1,R2,R4,R6,R7,R9 0 conflicts; R3 3 and R5 15 conflicts, none in .ros/

verification: driver unit tests 26/26 pass (dotnet fsi tests.fsx); harness unit tests 5/5 (python3 -m unittest); validate negative controls: dropped work item and dropped events detected, duplicated event line NOT detected; shallow-clone artifact found and re-run unshallowed
limitations: v2 relaxed-order rule was added after seeing v1 results (disclosed Amendment 1); not preregistered
driver is per-file: cannot bind both files to the same commits as Praxis's own resolver
actor policy (later updatedAt) differs from team choice in 17 R8 files; item/event ORDER differs from M in some files (team used ad hoc orders: R10 mostly sorted by ID)
only works for local merges; GitHub's server-side merge button and rebase-merge do not run custom drivers; drivers must be configured per clone (.git/config), .gitattributes alone is insufficient
dotnet fsi startup makes each driver call ~3-8 s; not optimized
2 of 26 logged R8 PR-merge replays and some R10 replays had criss-cross (multiple) merge bases; git built a virtual base, driver succeeded
praxis validate does not detect duplicate event lines
conclusion: SUPPORTED/VERIFIED for R8 and R10: v2 removed every .ros/ conflict (105 R8 + 65 R10 paths, 92 merges) with 0 lost and 0 duplicated records and passed praxis validate on all 92 results; it cannot touch the 9 merges with application/CI conflicts (4 in R8, 5 in R10).
reproduction: cd tools/ros-merge-driver && dotnet fsi tests.fsx; cd ../replay && python3 -m unittest test_replay_merges && python3 replay_merges.py <scratch-clone> <abs>/ros-merge.fsx ../../raw/targets-r8-all86.json out.jsonl && python3 summarize.py summary.json r8=out.jsonl && python3 validate_replays.py <scratch-clone2> <abs>/ros-merge.fsx <praxis-bin 3.24.0> ../../raw/targets-r8-all-ros.json val.jsonl (scratch clones must be unshallow)

question: What does rebuilding the pinned Praxis verifier cost, and can it be cached or replaced safely?
hypothesis: H1 cold >= 3x warm-incremental; H2 release fetch faster than cold build; H3 cache keyed on pin SHA (+OS, SDK, project) is correct
independentVars: build mode: cold (fresh tree, empty NuGet), warm-nuget (fresh tree, warm NuGet cache), warm-incremental (same tree), release fetch (download+verify+extract)
dependentVars: foundations verify JSON output and exit code
comparison: local timings vs CI step 'Build pinned Praxis verifier' (Track A ci-steps.csv); source-built verifier vs release v3.9.1 native bundle

environment.host: sandbox VM, 4 vCPU, 15 GB RAM, shared with other sprint tracks (1-min load avg 7-11 during builds)

verification: exit 0 for all 9 builds; same-path rebuild byte-identical; release asset sha256 equals GitHub digest; foundations verify JSON byte-identical source vs release on 4 rehearsal heads and on a negative control (both exit 3)
limitations: host shared with other tracks (load 7-11 on 4 vCPU); absolute local seconds are pessimistic vs GitHub runners (local cold is 1.53x CI median)
release fetch measured through the sandbox proxy, not from a GitHub runner
no release is tagged AT the pin; v3.9.1 is 2 commits later with no src/ change; release.json version string differs (3.9.1)
determinism probe is a single same-path rebuild
the dotnet-tool package EchelonFoundry.Praxis was not tested
conclusion: H1 SUPPORTED (cold/incremental ~20x; warm NuGet alone saves ~4%: compile-bound). H2 SUPPORTED (release fetch ~4.5 s vs ~93 s local cold / 61 s CI). H3 SUPPORTED with conditions: key must include pin SHA, runner OS/arch, SDK version and project path; output is path-dependent but reproducible at a fixed path. ESTIMATE ~550 of ~604 verifier minutes avoidable across R2-R10.
reproduction: tools/verifier-timing/time_builds.sh <git dir with pin> aa7c7ca6a6e2cb270bdccfe117ea35ade7b0945c <workdir> out.jsonl 3

question: How many CI minutes would fail-fast ordering (cheap gates before browser suites, browser jobs gated on them) have saved?
independentVars: counterfactual ordering model (within-job reorder; across-job needs-gating V1 expensive steps only, V2 whole job)
cheap-gate definition (broad = Track A categories build/test/static-gate; strict = excluding live/acceptance/provider/mutation/aggregate steps)
comparison: actual historical job/step durations vs counterfactual

environment.host: sandbox VM, 4 vCPU, 15 GB RAM, shared with other sprint tracks (1-min load avg 7-11 during builds)

rawResults.latencyPenaltyESTIMATE: median gating-job duration in green runs 55.5 s (n=106)

verification: unit tests on synthetic jobs; job-minute base reproduces Track A jobMinutesTotal (11,967.7)
limitations: counterfactual; assumes failure detected at the same step and that skipped jobs would not have been needed
cancelled jobs excluded (R10 20-minute timeouts get no saving)
result is dominated by R6 and highly sensitive to which steps count as cheap
does not model re-runs or developer wait
conclusion: INCONCLUSIVE: 23.7% of failed-run minutes (10.8% of all) under the preregistered broad definition, but only 5.9% (2.6%) when live/acceptance suites are not counted as cheap gates; most of the broad saving comes from R6.
